IN THE COURT OF THE CIVIL JUDGE (SENIOR DIVISION)
DEMO DISTRICT COURT, KAMRUP (METROPOLITAN), GUWAHATI

CIVIL SUIT NO. CS/1234/2026
CNR: DEMO010002026

Demo Petitioner A
        … Petitioner
    vs.
Demo Respondent B
        … Respondent

ORDER (Interim — 15 July 2026)

This matter was listed today for hearing on the application under Order XXXIX
Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

After hearing learned counsel for both sides and perusing the record, the Court
is of the prima facie view that the petitioner has made out a case for interim
protection of the suit property.

It is hereby ORDERED:

1. The respondent shall produce all original property-related documents,
   including the registered sale deed, mutation records, and land revenue
   receipts, before this Court within 30 (thirty) days from the date of
   this order.

2. Neither party shall alienate, encumber, or create any third-party interest
   in the suit property during the pendency of this suit.

3. The petitioner's counsel shall file written objections, if any, to the
   respondent's reply by 10 August 2026.

4. List for next hearing on 20 August 2026 at 10:30 AM in Court Room 4.

                                                    Sd/-
                                        Civil Judge (Senior Division)
                                        Demo District Court, Guwahati

step_2_explanation:
WHAT HAPPENED

This is an interim order — a temporary decision made while the full case is still being heard. The court has decided to protect the property in question until the final decision.

The case is between Demo Petitioner A (the person who filed the case) and Demo Respondent B (the person the case is against). It is being heard at the Demo District Court in Guwahati.

The court found that the petitioner has a reasonable case for protecting the property while the suit continues.

WHAT YOU MUST DO

1. The respondent must bring all original property papers to court within 30 days from 15 July 2026. This includes the sale deed (the document proving purchase), mutation records (land ownership transfer records), and land revenue receipts (proof of tax payments). The approximate deadline is 14 August 2026.

2. Neither side is allowed to sell, mortgage, or give any rights over the disputed property to anyone else while the case is going on.

3. The petitioner's lawyer must file written objections (formal disagreements with the respondent's reply) by 10 August 2026.

NEXT HEARING

The next hearing is on 20 August 2026 at 10:30 AM in Court Room 4.

WHAT IS NOT CLEAR

- The order does not state whether you must attend in person. Check with your lawyer or the court office to confirm whether personal attendance is needed on 20 August 2026.

- This is an interim order, not a final decision. The case will continue.

For free legal help, contact NALSA (National Legal Services Authority) or Tele-Law through the Department of Justice at doj.gov.in.
